result.title: Learning to Tune with Biased Gradients: Iterative Feedback Tuning of Model-Free Control on Throttle Valves
result.summary: Iterative feedback tuning (IFT) learns the parameters of a fixed-structure controller by stochastic gradient descent. At each iteration, two closed-loop experiments are run on the plant: the first one measures the tracking error, and the second one, driven by this error, provides the sensitivities from which the gradient of the cost is estimated. This estimate is unbiased for linear plants only. We study the biased case on automotive electronic throttle valves, whose friction and stiction vary between valves and runs, controlled by an intelligent proportional (model-free) controller, which is an incremental PI controller. We show that the mismatch of the controller state at the start of the two experiments, which stiction makes unavoidable, adds an error inversely proportional to the amplitude of the second experiment. On digital twins of ten valves, the IFT gradient is a descent direction in only 69\% of the low-cost region, friction being the cause, and all update rules plateau and then drift. On two hardware valves, the best update rule depends on the noise structure of the gradient. On the first valve, where one gradient component is buried in noise, Adam outperforms Gauss--Newton, its normalisation and its momentum each improving one parameter. On the second valve, where both components are consistent, the same normalisation amplifies a direction that Gauss--Newton rightly discounts, and Adam drifts to a controller worse than the initial one. The twins reproduce the mechanism but not this ranking.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究汽车电子节气门的迭代反馈整定（IFT），分析摩擦与爬行导致两次闭环实验初始状态不匹配、进而使梯度估计有偏的问题，并在数字孪生与两个硬件阀门上比较 Adam 与 Gauss–Newton 等更新规则的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是模型无关控制器的参数整定，与视觉/多模态推理中的内部表示、证据获取和 latent 状态生成无实质联系；文中「梯度噪声结构决定更新规则优劣」仅属泛化优化经验，难以形成针对 LVR 训练监督或贡献分配的具体借鉴线索。
